- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates price spikes in the next 5–10 days — apply a small upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.5%) to forecast peaks.  
- Model overestimates mean reversion in short-term (1–3 days) — reduce forecast magnitude for immediate next-day moves.  
- If sentiment shifts sharply from negative to positive within 3 days, model lags — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of true breakout.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates final price — add 0.5–1.5% to final forecast to account for tail risk and momentum carry.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
